simple.meaning: מֵיטָב (mêyṭâb) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “the best part.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 47:6. The surrounding context includes family, sacrifice, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֵיטָב (H4315) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מֵיטָב (mêyṭâb) / H4315 is traced through Genesis 47:6, Genesis 47:11, Exodus 22:4, 1 Samuel 15:9 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: The land of Egypt is before you. Make your father and your brothers dwell in the best of the land. Let them dwell in the land of Goshen. If you know any able men among them, then put them in charge of my livestock.”
Joseph placed his father and his brothers, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, of the cattle, and of the fat calves, and the lambs, and all that was good, and were not willing to utterly destroy them; but everything that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly.
Saul said, “They have brought them from the Amalekites; for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the cattle, to sacrifice to Yahweh your God. We have utterly destroyed the rest.”

definitions.full: H4315. metab ( מֵיטָב ) noun [masculine] the best , only construct מֵיטַב and as superlative; the best of a thing: כָּרְמוֺ ׳מ וּמ ׳שָׂדֵהוּ Exod 22:4 (JE) the best of his field and the best of his vineyard (choicest fruit); ׳מ הַצּאֹן the best of the sheep 1Sam 15:9 , 15 ; ׳בְּמ הָאָרֶץ in the best of the land Gen 47:6 , 11 (P). יוּטָה יֻטָּה, see below נטה . יְטוּר see below טוּר . יין (√ of following; meaning unknown; regarded as loan-word by Lag Armen. Stud. § 484 and others; Hom ZMG 1889, 653 ff.; Aufsätze, 1892, 102 compare Georgian g'wino , wine whence also (according to him) Armenian gini , Greek οῖνος , Latin vinum ; compare on the other hand Jen l.c. below )
